blocks.content: An appeal to the High Court lies only if the case involves a substantial question of law.

items: Remember the monetary limits for filing departmental appeals before ITAT, High Court, and Supreme Court.
ITAT is the ultimate fact-finding body; High Court does not re-examine pure questions of fact.
The statutory time period for filing an appeal before CIT(A) is 30 days from the date of service of the demand notice.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first appeal against an order of the Assessing Officer lies with the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)].
An appeal against the order of CIT(A) can be preferred before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) within 60 days of order communication.
ITAT is the final fact-finding authority; questions of fact cannot be appealed beyond the Tribunal.
An appeal to the High Court against an ITAT order lies only on a substantial question of law.
The Supreme Court serves as the highest court of appeal against High Court orders via special leave or certification.
